problems.source_says: The final form is more conservative than the conclusion in the brief: it codes criterion 2 as unclear. However, Supplementary Figure 8a displays analyzed human nodes in Study A's four mixed human-agent conditions: 21 at 12.5% (H_0 through H_20), 16 at 33.3% (H_0 through H_15), 12 at 50% (H_0 through H_11), and 6 at 75% (H_0 through H_5). These are counts of individually labeled blue human nodes, verified visually in the PDF, not counts of edges, descriptions, agents, or repeated rounds. The caption identifies each node as a participant, and the accompanying method computes each participant's influence from their description changes. The derived total is 21 + 16 + 12 + 6 = 55 humans analyzed within Study A; assignment to one of eight conditions establishes that these four arms are distinct. This establishes criterion 2 without treating all 79 allocated Study A humans as confirmed consensus-analysis completers. Exact consensus-specific analyzed counts can remain null.
problems.quote: Directed influence networks constructed from pairwise interaction data. Each node represents a participant (blue: human, red: agent), with node size proportional to reverse PageRank.
problems.locator: PDF p. 28, Supplementary Figure 8a, four labeled influence networks and caption; PDF pp. 20-21, Influence Network Analysis; PDF p. 16, Participants, random assignment to one condition and Study A allocation roster. The human-node counts are derived from the figure, not a printed sample-size total.

confirmed.statement: Human participants were randomly assigned to one of eight experimental conditions spanning Studies A-C; round-by-round partner rematching is a separate randomization.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 16, Participants and Game Procedure.

confirmed.statement: Study A human allocation counts are 24, 21, 16, 12, and 6 for 0%, 12.5%, 33.3%, 50%, and 75% agents, respectively, matching every recorded arm n_randomized. Their derived sum is 79 randomized humans, not a separately printed analyzed total.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 16, Participants, Study A allocation sentence.

confirmed.statement: Study B allocates 16 humans to high-adoption and 16 to high-persistence agents; Study C allocates 16 to the smaller-model condition. These match the three new-condition arm counts in the form.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 16, Participants, Study B and Study C allocation sentences.

confirmed.statement: The reported 127 is the recruited human total across the paper. The eight unique allocation counts sum to 127 (79 + 16 + 16 + 16); 127 must not be used as a single study analyzed N.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 16, Participants, recruitment statement and eight-condition roster; sums are derived.

confirmed.statement: A session contains 24 players including both humans and AI agents, with the same players interacting over 40 rounds. Neither the mixed-player N of 24 nor repeated descriptions, pairs, or rounds should be counted as additional humans.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 16, Game Procedure; PDF p. 7, Methods M1; PDF p. 21, influence-network N.

confirmed.statement: Study A has at least 55 analyzed humans in its influence-network analysis: the four mixed-arm networks contain 21, 16, 12, and 6 individually labeled human nodes. The analysis derives influence from produced descriptions; it is not merely a planned allocation diagram.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 20-21, Influence Network Analysis; PDF p. 28, Supplementary Figure 8a-c, visually inspected human nodes, distributions, and caption.

confirmed.statement: Supplementary Table 1 reports N = 495 questionnaire regression observations, not 495 people. Each person supplied one adoption-willingness rating for each of nine sampled interactions; 495 / 9 = 55 is a consistency check, not a substitute for the figure-based human count or a consensus-analysis N.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 29, Supplementary Table 1; PDF pp. 5 and 17, nine sampled interactions and one willingness response per interaction; PDF p. 9, Methods M5.

confirmed.statement: Enrollment required passing English-expression, expression-diversity, and task-comprehension screening. The number screened out is unreported; no numerical post-randomization exclusion or attrition flow is supplied. The procedure says each human filled out the questionnaire after completing 40 rounds, but gives no separate outcome-specific completion totals.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 16, Participants and Post-experiment Questionnaire; full markdown and appendices reviewed through PDF p. 29.

confirmed.statement: Exact analyzed-human counts for the consensus outcome, the pure-human baseline, and the additional Study B/C conditions are not separately reported. The observed Study A network counts do not establish a universal 79-person consensus-analysis N or zero exclusions on every outcome.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 7-9, Methods; PDF p. 16, allocation roster; PDF pp. 20-21 and 28, network analysis; PDF p. 29, the only supplementary table.

confirmed.statement: Failed LLM content annotations can be recorded as missing after three retries; this is output-level missingness, with no reported count of excluded human participants.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 19, Content Annotation Using LLM-as-a-Judge.

confirmed.statement: Studies B and C compare against the neutral 33.3%/32B condition, but the allocation roster lists that condition only once, in Study A. Internal reuse is strongly indicated rather than explicitly declared; the form appropriately warns against counting its 16 humans as independently recruited again. Conditional on sharing, comparison-wide allocations would be 48 for B and 32 for C, both below 50, not confirmed analyzed totals.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, trait and model comparisons; PDF p. 14, Figure 3d-g; PDF p. 16, eight-condition allocation roster. Conditional totals are derived.

confirmed.statement: No reuse of these human participants from another paper is disclosed. This verifies absence of a reuse statement, not independently established non-overlap with all other papers.
confirmed.locator: Full document, including PDF p. 16, Participants, and PDF pp. 10-11, references; all supplementary material through p. 29 reviewed.

summary: Study A's supplementary influence-network analysis includes 55 humans, so criterion 2 holds. The form's 'unclear' criterion-2 coding is refuted; its printed allocation counts are correct, while exact consensus-specific analyzed totals remain unconfirmed.
